title: Field ask skein and runtime hypotheses - synthesis
content:
Quick note: pulled ~92 raw threads from support, solutions engineering, and pilot accounts (period: 2026-09 -> 2026-11). This doc is a lightweight synthesis aimed at: 1) surfacing repeat runtime friction patterns, 2) proposing low-effort mitigations (0-2 sprints), and 3) sketching experiment hypotheses for product/engineering pairing.

Topline summary:
- Three recurring friction clusters: KV cache invalidation & warmup pain, tokenization/encoding mismatches across SDKs, and unexpected latency spikes during small-batch bursts. Together they account for ~63% of the operational complaints (by mention count) and ~74% of customer-reported incident minutes in the dataset.
- Quick wins exist (edge config toggles, client-side retry guidance, SDK short-patch) that likely reduce noise by ~30-50% while longer-term runtime fixes (cache persistence and routing heuristics) need deeper infra work.

Signal clusters (with representative vignettes):
1) KV cache & warm start fragility (27 mentions)
  - Vignette: Retail analytics client reports repeated cold-start latencies after model rollouts; they observed 2-6x token latency for first 100 requests post-deploy.
  - Root causes (hypothesized): cache eviction policies too aggressive for low-traffic pods; canary deploys cause model sharding that invalidates KV prefixes.
  - Customer ask examples: persistent per-tenant cache, option to pin warmup tokens, visibility into cache hit/miss per-route.

2) Tokenization and encoding mismatches (21 mentions)
  - Vignette: Multi-lingual customer sending UTF-8 sequences that the client lib normalizes differently than backend, resulting in different token counts and unexpected billing.
  - Ask: deterministic SDK normalization, clear docs/example for pre-tokenization, server-side detection with explainable warnings.

3) Micro-burst latency spikes (18 mentions)
  - Vignette: A B2B search app sees occasional 200-600ms tail spikes during very low concurrency with concurrent small batches (N=2-5).
  - Hypothesis: autoscaler cold-pools and suboptimal batching heuristics at sequence length distribution tails.

Low-effort mitigations (0-2 sprints) — prioritized by expected impact / effort:
- SDK patch: expose explicit normalization utility and option to pre-tokenize in client. Low effort. Owner: devx. Jira: JIRA-INF-8721.
- Admin toggle: "backend soft-warm" per-deployment flag that sends 20 warmup tokens on first allocation. Medium-low effort (config + small warmup task).
- KB article + support template: 'How to reduce transient latency after rollouts' with step-by-step for customers + automated snippet generation for SEs. Very low effort.

Experiment / mid-term hypotheses (2-6 sprints):
- Persistent tenant-local KV cache (opt-in): maintain a small SSD-backed KV cache per-tenant with TTL lanes; measure cold-start percentiles. Success metric: reduce p95 cold-start latency by 40% for pilot tenants. Linked PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/458 (prototype).
- Routing policy tweak: prefer warmed nodes for canaries when traffic ratio < 5%; evaluate throughput and isolation tradeoffs. Metric: incident count vs. baseline over 2 weeks.

Customer-prioritized feature requests (annotated):
- "Per-route cache metrics" (High impact, medium effort) — customers want token-level cache hit/miss + time-since-last-warm. Suggested acceptance criteria: per-route dashboard tile + exportable CSV.
- "SDK deterministic normalization" (High impact, low effort) — explicit behavior across platforms + test vectors.
- "Burst-aware autoscaling profile" (Medium impact, medium effort) — tuning options for small-batch burst workloads.

Engineering notes & constraints:
- Serving runtime: cache changes risk increasing disk I/O — must simulate under realistic traffic (use existing perf harness, see CONFLUENCE-2345).
- Any per-tenant persistence requires KMS alignment for private deployments (security review flagged).

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we want to ship a backend soft-warm toggle as an interim solution or push directly to persistent cache? (Trade: quicker noise reduction vs. technical debt).
- Can devx commit to a minor SDK release in the next sprint? Need slot in sprint planning.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Maya: Draft KB + support template (ETA 2026-11-12).
- Jonah (SE): Run two pilot warmup experiments with retail & search pilot tenants, gather p95/p99 (ETA 2026-11-24).
- Engineering: Triage JIRA-INF-8721 and estimate SDK patch (ETA: rough estimate 3 days).
- Product: Decide soft-warm vs. persistent-cache prioritization in next roadmap meeting (2026-11-17).

Notes to self / ephemeral:
- Collected raw quotes in GS sheet: "support-bed/kv-cold-starts-2026-11" (internal).
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-friction (see thread ts: 2026-11-02T16:04).

Appendix — quick example support text for SEs (can be copy/pasted):
"If you’re seeing latency spikes right after deploys, try enabling the soft-warm toggle in the deployment UI or run the client warmup script we provide in the support article. If issues persist, capture the first-100 request latency trace and attach to ticket JIRA-INF-8721. Include SDK version and sample payloads (pre/post normalization)."

End notes: this doc is intentionally compact. If we want, follow-up draft can expand into a playbook (ops+SE runbook) and a small perf experiment plan (harness configs, datasets, tenants).
